title: 伊達成実の家臣団
summary: 一応、苗字のアイウエオ順。なぜ「一応」かというと、読みに自信がないから。成実の生存期間中に、活動の記載のある家臣を収録しています。

en.title: Retainers of Shigezane Date
en.summary: Listed, for now, in alphabetical order by surname. The reason I say "for now" is that I'm not entirely sure of the readings. This list includes retainers whose activities are recorded during Shigezane's lifetime.
en.html:
Listed roughly in alphabetical order by surname. The reason I say "roughly" is that I'm not entirely confident in the readings. This list includes retainers whose activities are recorded during Shigezane's lifetime. Reference materials: "Watari Yoshin Kafu Ryakki," "Masamune-ki," "Kyodo Watari Nos. 81, 57, 46," "Teizan-ko Jika Kiroku," "Date Tensho Nikki," "Kuranosuke Yashiki," "Date Yoshin Kafu," "Shihon Sendai-han Shi Jiten," "Watari-machi Shi," "Sendai-han Kashinroku," "Genealogies of the Katakura Clan, Lords of Shiroishi Castle, and Their Retainers," "Watari Date Family Documents Research Group Results Report 1: Catalog of Documents from Various Houses of the Watari Date Clan held at Daiyu-ji Temple in Hokkaido, with 'Oshu Soma-shi Nomaoi-zu Byobu' held by Date City." Information provided by: Haru-sama, Tome@Date-otoko-sama

※1 Number from the Watari Yoshin Kafu Ryakki. Represents the rank at the time the Watari Yoshin Kafu Ryakki was compiled.

※2 Distinctions between Bajo (horse), Toko (on foot), Fudan-teppo (non-iron), Shinchi-bajo (new horse), Shinchi-go-toko (new foot), Go-fudan-gumi (non-iron), Go-kachi-ko-me-tsurau-go-kachu (So), and Iwaki-gozen-sama-me-tsurau-go-kachu (Iwa), according to the Warabi Shishido Family Documents (as published in "Kyodo Watari No. 57"). This is said to be a copy made in Genroku 11 from the original of Kan'ei 19.

Aoki Yamato-no-kami

  • Appears in the Tensho Diary as a messenger "from Nihonmatsu (Shigezane)." May have been a direct retainer of Masamune.

Aoki Genban-no-jo

  • A retainer of Toshimune Kakeda. The Sawajiri clan was related to him. In Genki 2, he served under Sanemoto. In Tensho 4, he distinguished himself at the Battle of Kawamata and was granted a letter of commendation by Terumune.

Aoki Tanetsuna

  • Danjo-no-chu. Son of Aoki Genban-no-jo. Played an active role in negotiations with the Tamura clan.

Tsunahiro Aoki

  • Bizen. Son of Aoki Tanetsuna. During the Battle of Hitotoribashi, he served as the castle warden of Obama Castle. When Shigezane fled, he became a direct retainer of Masamune and was granted 200 koku. He resided in Narita Village, Otani-sho, Kurokawa District, as a district magistrate. His descendants were common samurai of the Sendai Domain.
  • Participated in the takeover of Kakuda Castle during Shigezane's flight (Sendai Shiryo "Shigezane Date Fled to Takano")

Shigejiro Asanuma

  • Served in the Summer Campaign of the Siege of Osaka (on foot).

Sokuro Asanuma

Sanemitsu Ishikawa

  • Participated as a military commander in the Battle of Osaki (Oshu Kasai Jikki)
  • The entry for Tanemitsu, the 23rd head, in the "Thousand-Year History of the Ishikawa Clan" states: "Third son, Mitsuteru; mother, Chosho-in. Known as Fukuda Kosaburo. Lord of Shinjo Castle in Mogami District, Ushu Province; served Ashikaga Shuri-no-daibu Minamoto no Yoshimori Asomi. Known as Ishikawa Yahei. Son, Mitsutomo, served the Date clan during the Tensho era."

Mitsusada Ishikawa

  • Kageyu, Genbei, Sanuki. Eldest son of Ishikawa Tanba, the younger brother of Ishikawa Danjo Hisakuni. During the fall of Kokotemori Castle, he escaped disguised as a laborer, sought the aid of Suzuki Inaba, and entered the service of Shigezane. Later, in Tensho 16, he entered the service of Kagetsuna Katakura, serving as a ronin. (Genealogy of the Katakura clan, lords of Shiroishi Castle, and their retainers)

Ishigaki Tarozaemon

  • Resident since the Genna era. Ishigaya.
  • (History of Watari Town, p. 318)

Tanba Ito

  • Brief Genealogy of the Watari Yoshin Family 120: Michimune. Around the time of Shigezane, he was summoned to serve as a mounted guard. He distinguished himself as a vanguard during the siege of Kanayama Castle. He was granted the Kanayama gate and served as the imperial comb-bearer. He excelled in the use of a powerful bow.

Hiromasa Ibano

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 23: Shiroemon. Totomi. When Sanemoto entered the Uesugi clan, he was assigned to Sanemoto and granted a hikaryo-mon torige-tai-yari and a Bizen nagasaki nagamitsu by Uemune. He played a prominent role despite his advanced age in the Battle of Hitotoribashi, where he was killed in action. Served as a karo.
  • Their ancestors accompanied the Date clan during their descent to Oshu (Bunji 5) and served as hereditary elders.
  • Landholdings: Higashine, Date District (residence, 1 ken); Awano (field within Himukai, 1 kanmon); Yashiro (Aimori Mameda, 100 kari); Shimo-Yanome (residence, 1 ken); within Kasajima-go, Igu-sho)

Hiroyoshi Ibano

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 23: Kurado-no-jo. Genki 2–Kan'ei 17. During the Koriyama standoff in Tensho 17, he was struck in the nape of the neck by a musket ball but survived. He never removed the ball for the rest of his life, twisting it as a source of amusement while drinking. It is said that, in accordance with his will, the ball was removed after his death and placed in an armor chest.
  • Camped at the Mogami camp (on horseback).

Ushisaka Sado

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 25: In his father's generation, he left the Hojo clan and entered the service of Date Naomune after the Eisho Campaign. He was adopted into Sado and was actually the second son of Horikoshi Noto. He held a fief of 500 koku. When Sanemoto succeeded to the Uesugi clan, he was assigned 30 mounted riders as a samurai commander and was placed under Sanemoto's command. He subsequently became a retainer of Sanemoto.
  • Various holdings: Ushizaka, Date District (all but the portion allocated to Makino Danjo), Yamanokawa (1 ken), Ishinasaka, Shinobu District (Hirasawa Kurosawa residence and horse stable, 1 ken)

Sanetaka Ushizaka

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 25: Sakon. Son of Ushizaka Sado. He served in Shigezane's battles and achieved military merit.

Ushisaka Sado

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 25: Son of Sanetaka Ushizaka.

Koryu Ushizaka

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 25: Kishiro. Later Kizaemon. Son of Ushizaka Sado. Had an audience with Masamune at Wakabayashi Castle in Sendai. In recognition of his grandfather Sanetaka's military achievements, he was granted a sake cup and a wakizashi belonging to Kunimune. Ordered by Masamune to change his name to Kizaemon, he accordingly changed his name.

Sagenta Ushizaka

  • On Horseback (Warabi Shishido Family Documents)

Mototaka Uchizaki

  • Uma-no-kami. Mimasaka. Echigo. His father, Kai Kaneshige, was a member of the Osaki clan. After his remonstrances went unheeded, he left the Osaki house. Through Shigezane, he requested appointment as a retainer to the Date clan. Uma-no-kami Mototaka negotiated with Ogoshi Kii-no-kami regarding the succession dispute in Tamura. Later, he was summoned by Masamune for 20 kanmon and changed his name to Mimasaka. He became a senior retainer to Date Hidemune, but due to a falling out, he returned to his home province and changed his name to Echigo. His lineage became extinct in Horeki 9.
  • During the Bunroku era, along with Haneda Umanosuke and Endo Shukei, he served as the caretaker of Kakuda (Sendai Shiryo, "Shigezane Date Flees to Takano")
  • Participated in the takeover of Kakuda Castle during Shigezane's flight (Sendai Shiryo "Shigezane Date Fled to Takano")

Kazue Endo

  • September 5, Bunroku 2: Memorial services were held for Endo Shimotsuke at Koyasan Kannon-in. (Included in City History Sendai vol. 12, "Koyasan Kannon-in Kakocho, Otsu-bon")
  • September 5, Bunroku 2: Memorial services were held for the repose of Asanuma Sokuro at Koyasan Kannon-in. (Included in City History of Sendai, Vol. 12, "Koyasan Kannon-in Kakocho, Otsu-bon")
  • Participated in the takeover of Kakuda Castle during Shigezane's flight (Sendai Shiryo "Shigezane Date Fled to Takano")

Endo Suruga-no-kami

  • In Tensho 16, when Sadatsuna submitted to the Date clan, he accompanied Sadatsuna to Masamune (Jike Kiroku).
  • Sent a letter to an acquaintance of the enemy during the standoff at Koriyama.
  • The Endo family of the Sendai Domain's main hall records "Endo Suruga" as the head of the house during the Eiroku period. During the time of the Awano Daizen administration, he went to Natori and resided in Kawakami Village for several years. For some reason, his ancestral estate was extinguished; during the Keicho era, Fujizaemon, the heir of Suruga, petitioned the Date main house for service and was granted permission.
  • See Date Masamune Documents 162
  • Quoted from Rikka (Oral traditions of "Shinobu Village," Fukushima City). The mountain on the border between Oda and Hiraishi is known as either Asahi-kan or Shinchi-kan. It is said that during the time of Terumune Date, Endo Suruga-no-kami, a retainer of the Date clan, lived here; traces such as dry moats still remain in the mountains today. (From "History of Fukushima City," Supplemental Volume IV: Folklore of Fukushima II (Place Names))

Yasukiyo Okabe

  • Hoki. Grandson of Okabe Suruga-no-kami, a former retainer of Ashina. His father, Okuma, provided lodging to Shigezane in Kyoto; through this connection, Okabe entered the service of Masamune upon Shigezane's recommendation and was granted 700 koku. During the tenure of Hoki Yasukiyo, he committed a crime and had his lands confiscated, after which he resided in Shirane. In Genna 9, he was pardoned and moved to Watari, where he received a retirement stipend of 50 nin-fuchi. The Okabe family was inherited by his brother-in-law, who became a retainer of the Sendai Domain.
  • Okabe Naizen, the founder of the Kishiwada Domain, is said to be the younger brother of Okuma, but there is no mention of Okuma or Suruga in the Kishiwada Domain's Kansei-fu. (History of Kakuda City 2) See → Buke Kaden - Okabe Clan
  • My great-grandfather, Okabe Osumi, of the Aizu fudai line, fell from power in that region; thereafter, through the mediation of Shigezane Date, he was summoned by Lord Teizan... As for the matter of Osumi's biological son, Hoki, he was subject to a lawsuit by Shigezane and was granted a fief within the domain in Genna 9; he resided in Watari under Shigezane's care and died of illness there on December 29, Shoho 4. His son, my father Okabe Arisetsu, was also a ronin and resided in the same place... (Enpo Shojo 26-9, Okabe Gensetsu)

Naotsugu Tadaki

  • Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 53: Echigo. Tensho 10 (1582)–Shoho 3 (1646). Served Shigezane. Also known as Naosada. After entering Watari, he became embroiled in an argument with other senior retainers within the castle, which led to his attainder and exile. Three years later, he was recalled; not only were his lands and holdings restored to their former status, but he also received the income he had earned during his exile. Overcome with gratitude, he devoted himself to loyal service as a mounted guard. During the era of great peace, as there were no battles in which his life could be risked, he requested and was granted permission to commit ritual suicide (junshi), and was presented with the sake cup for the oath of ritual suicide (tsuihara go-seiyaku). It is said that Shigezane frequently visited Naotsugu's retirement residence to view his horses. After Shigezane's death, he visited Daiyu-ji Temple three times a day and committed ritual suicide on June 20. His Buddhist name was Kan-o Totetsu. His death poem: "The clouds of my heart have cleared, and I am now truly beholding the light of the moon."

Listed roughly in alphabetical order by surname. The reason I say "roughly" is that I'm not entirely confident in the readings. This list includes retainers whose activities are recorded during Shigezane's lifetime. Reference materials: "Watari Yoshin Kafu Ryakki," "[Masamune-ki](#/post/shigezane/tyosaku)," "Kyodo Watari Nos. 81, 57, 46," "Teizan-ko Jika Kiroku," "Date Tensho Nikki," "[Kuranosuke Yashiki](http://www.page.sannet.ne.jp/kuranosuke/index.html)," "Date Yoshin Kafu," "Shihon Sendai-han Shi Jiten," "Watari-machi Shi," "Sendai-han Kashinroku," "Genealogies of the Katakura Clan, Lords of Shiroishi Castle, and Their Retainers," "Watari Date Family Documents Research Group Results Report 1: Catalog of Documents from Various Houses of the Watari Date Clan held at Daiyu-ji Temple in Hokkaido, with 'Oshu Soma-shi Nomaoi-zu Byobu' held by Date City." Information provided by: Haru-sama, Tome@Date-otoko-sama

※1 Number from the Watari Yoshin Kafu Ryakki. Represents the rank at the time the Watari Yoshin Kafu Ryakki was compiled.

※2 Distinctions between Bajo (horse), Toko (on foot), Fudan-teppo (non-iron), Shinchi-bajo (new horse), Shinchi-go-toko (new foot), Go-fudan-gumi (non-iron), Go-kachi-ko-me-tsurau-go-kachu (So), and Iwaki-gozen-sama-me-tsurau-go-kachu (Iwa), according to the Warabi Shishido Family Documents (as published in "Kyodo Watari No. 57"). This is said to be a copy made in Genroku 11 from the original of Kan'ei 19.

### Aoki Yamato-no-kami

- Danjo-no-chu. Son of Aoki Genban-no-jo. Played an active role in negotiations with the Tamura clan.

- Bizen. Son of Aoki Tanetsuna. During the Battle of Hitotoribashi, he served as the castle warden of Obama Castle. When Shigezane fled, he became a direct retainer of Masamune and was granted 200 koku. He resided in Narita Village, Otani-sho, Kurokawa District, as a district magistrate. His descendants were common samurai of the Sendai Domain.

The mountain on the border between Oda and Hiraishi is known as either Asahi-kan or Shinchi-kan. It is said that during the time of Terumune Date, Endo Suruga-no-kami, a retainer of the Date clan, lived here; traces such as dry moats still remain in the mountains today. ### Naotsugu Tadaki

- Brief Record of the Watari Yoshin Family Genealogy 53: Echigo. Tensho 10 (1582)–Shoho 3 (1646). Served Shigezane. Also known as Naosada. After entering Watari, he became embroiled in an argument with other senior retainers within the castle, which led to his attainder and exile. Three years later, he was recalled; not only were his lands and holdings restored to their former status, but he also received the income he had earned during his exile. Overcome with gratitude, he devoted himself to loyal service as a mounted guard. During the era of great peace, as there were no battles in which his life could be risked, he requested and was granted permission to commit ritual suicide (junshi), and was presented with the sake cup for the oath of ritual suicide (tsuihara go-seiyaku). It is said that Shigezane frequently visited Naotsugu's retirement residence to view his horses. After Shigezane's death, he visited Daiyu-ji Temple three times a day and committed ritual suicide on June 20. His Buddhist name was Kan-o Totetsu. His death poem: "The clouds of my heart have cleared, and I am now truly beholding the light of the moon."

一応、苗字のアイウエオ順。なぜ「一応」かというと、読みに自信がないから。\
成実の生存期間中に、活動の記載のある家臣を収録しています。\
参考資料：「亘理世臣家譜略記」「[政宗記](#/post/shigezane/tyosaku)」「郷土わたり81号、57号、46号」「貞山公治家記録」「伊達天正日記」[「くらのすけ屋敷」](http://www.page.sannet.ne.jp/kuranosuke/index.html)「伊達世臣家譜」 「私本仙台藩士事典」「亘理町史」「仙台藩家臣録」 「白石城主片倉氏と家臣の系譜」「亘理伊達家文書調査研究会成果報告書1 北海道大雄寺所蔵 亘理伊達家中諸家文書目録 附伊達市所蔵「奥州相馬氏野馬追図屏風」」\
情報提供：ハルさま とめ＠伊達男さま

※1 亘理世臣家譜略記の番号。亘理世臣家譜略記成立時の序列をあらわす。

※2 蕨宍戸家文書（「郷土わたり57号」掲載分）による馬上（馬）・徒行（歩）・不断鉄砲（不鉄）・新地馬上（新馬）・新地御徒行（新歩）・御不断組（不）・宗実公召連候御家中（宗）・岩城御前様召連候御家中（岩）の別。寛永19年の原本を元禄11年に写したものという。

### 青木大和守

- 天正日記に「二本松（成実）より」の使いとして登場。政宗直臣の可能性もあり。

### 青木玄蕃允

- 懸田俊宗の臣。[沢尻氏](#/post/shigezane/kasin)は一族。元亀2年実元に属す。天正4年川俣の戦いに功あり。輝宗より感状を賜う。

### 青木胤綱

- 弾正忠。青木玄蕃允の子。田村家との交渉に活躍。

### 青木綱広

- 備前。青木胤綱の子。人取橋合戦の際、小浜城留守居を務める。成実出奔時に政宗の直臣となり、200石を受ける。郡代として黒川郡大谷庄成田村に住む。子孫は仙台藩平士。
- 成実出奔時の角田城接収に参加（[仙台志料「伊達成実高野に遁る」](#/post/shigezane/sendaishiryou-1)）

### 内崎元隆

### 但木直次

- 亘理世臣家譜略記53 越後。天正10（1582）～正保3（1646）。成実に仕える。直定とも。 亘理入府後、城中で他の重臣と口論になり、それが元で改易の上追放の憂き目に。3年後に呼び戻され、元通りに知行安堵された上に、追放中の収入も貰ったので感激して忠勤に励む。馬上番身合として奉公。 大平の世の中で身命を投げ打つ戦もないので、殉死を願い出て許され、追腹御誓約の盃を賜る。 直次の隠居屋敷には度々成実が馬を見に訪れたと言う。 成実の死後、大雄寺に日に三度ずつ参詣拝礼し、6月20日に殉死。法名関翁透鉄。辞世「おのづからすます心の雲はれて まことの月のひかりをぞ見る」

  • 亘理世臣家譜略記53 越後。天正10（1582）～正保3（1646）。成実に仕える。直定とも。 亘理入府後、城中で他の重臣と口論になり、それが元で改易の上追放の憂き目に。3年後に呼び戻され、元通りに知行安堵された上に、追放中の収入も貰ったので感激して忠勤に励む。馬上番身合として奉公。 大平の世の中で身命を投げ打つ戦もないので、殉死を願い出て許され、追腹御誓約の盃を賜る。 直次の隠居屋敷には度々成実が馬を見に訪れたと言う。 成実の死後、大雄寺に日に三度ずつ参詣拝礼し、6月20日に殉死。法名関翁透鉄。辞世「おのづからすます心の雲はれて まことの月のひかりをぞ見る」
